expertise: reliability, migration, testing, and infrastructure rule validation

voters.role: Senior Skill Architecture & Reference Governance Reviewer
expertise: Skill architecture, Reference governance, authority boundaries, semantic detectors, and progressive disclosure

ballot_rationales.rationale: Within diagnostic evidence-freshness work, remembered claims are selectors rather than proof; letting them overrule current source or fresh operations would make an agent preserve stale causality.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: The failure-diagnosis evidence-freshness contract when a remembered claim conflicts with current repository evidence or fresh operational evidence.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Treat memory as a hypothesis, record conflicts, distinguish current source from deployed state, and prefer fresh operational evidence for runtime facts.

ballot_rationales.rationale: Within freshness-sensitive diagnosis, remembered claims are unverified selectors; allowing them to override current source or fresher operational observations would permit stale causality and closure claims.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Failure diagnosis where a remembered claim conflicts with current source or fresher operational evidence for the same scope and time window.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Record provenance and timestamps, reconcile source with deployed-state evidence, and preserve explicit proof limits when current source and operations disagree.

ballot_rationales.rationale: The absolute word marks a deliberate evidence-precedence rule, not a blanket process ban. During failure diagnosis, remembered context may guide inspection but cannot supersede current source or fresh operational evidence without making the conclusion stale.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies while failure-diagnosis evaluates current repository state or fresh operational evidence against remembered context.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Keep memory selector-only, record contradictions, and retain an unresolved status when fresh evidence is missing.

ballot_rationales.rationale: The detector matched four shared label names, while all eleven blocks provide owner-specific strong, weak, missing, and invalid evidence. The stable taxonomy improves interpretation without duplicating one decision procedure.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Foundation evidence-pattern References that share evidence-quality vocabulary while keeping domain-specific examples, invalid states, and proof limits local to each owner.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Keep the four labels stable, require domain-specific bodies, and re-review if the bodies converge into generic boilerplate or a selectively loadable shared contract replaces them.

ballot_rationales.rationale: The detector correctly sees a repeated four-label evidence schema, but the eleven occurrences populate it with distinct owner-specific strength, absence, invalidity, and proof-limit criteria rather than a generic mandated workflow.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Evidence-pattern References whose four shared quality labels are populated with capability-specific evidence and failure criteria.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Keep each occurrence owner-specific; re-review the group if rows converge into generic boilerplate or duplicate a second operational checklist.

ballot_rationales.rationale: The repeated four labels form a shared evidence-quality taxonomy, while each of the 11 References supplies domain-specific rows and proof expectations. Common labels support comparable handoffs without replacing owner-specific professional content.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies only to indexed evidence-pattern References whose owner-specific rows classify strong, weak, missing, and invalid proof.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Retain the shared labels only while the rows remain domain-specific; re-review if the block expands into duplicated generic prose.

ballot_rationales.rationale: Repair closure against the latest diff and fresh validation prevents an agent from approving a superseded patch or reusing evidence invalidated by later edits.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: An L5 repair or re-review in which an existing finding is being closed as repaired rather than withdrawn, accepted, or reclassified.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Apply this only to repair closure; record withdrawn, accepted, or reclassified findings through their distinct decision path and evidence.

ballot_rationales.rationale: In the repair-and-re-review branch, closure against the latest repair diff and post-repair validation prevents superseded artifacts or pre-fix green results from being treated as evidence of repair.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: A blocking implementation finding being closed as repaired after a material code, configuration, fixture, or generated-artifact change.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Use relevant fresh validation and independent re-review; record invalidation or explicit risk acceptance through its separate disposition instead of labeling it repaired.

ballot_rationales.rationale: A repaired finding can be closed only against the changed repair state and fresh validation; earlier diffs or evidence cannot establish that the reported defect is gone. The rule is scoped to repair closure within independent code review.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies when ai-code-review-refactor decides whether a previously reported finding is closed after a repair.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Re-review the latest repair diff with fresh validation and keep the finding open when either artifact is unavailable.

ballot_rationales.rationale: The word only occurs inside quoted dependency-claim labels. The sentence classifies those claims as scoped assertions; it does not impose an unconditional only-rule on agent behavior.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Dependency evidence classification where quoted phrases such as dev only and not reachable are claim text awaiting scope and freshness proof.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Retain the quotation and scope language, and calibrate future detection to ignore absolute tokens that occur only inside quoted claim labels.

ballot_rationales.rationale: The matched word only is inside the quoted claim ‘dev only’; it is claim text being scoped for evidence review, not an unconditional restriction or mandated dependency mechanism.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Dependency evidence review of quoted reachability, environment, approval, and license claims.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Require current package path, version, reachability, license, advisory data, and validation before accepting any quoted claim.

ballot_rationales.rationale: The detector token occurs inside the quoted claim "dev only". The sentence does not impose an unconditional mechanism; it classifies several common dependency assertions as scoped claims that require supporting path, version, reachability, approval, or license evidence.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies during dependency-vulnerability review when a supplied assertion attempts to narrow exposure, approval, or license scope.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Retain the claim-scope verification and re-run semantic review if the quoted examples become a universal operating rule.

ballot_rationales.rationale: All is embedded in the quoted, unscoped label all users that the rule rejects. It is not a quantifier commanding behavior across every user or task.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: User-role identification anti-pattern guidance where an unqualified all-users label is rejected until actor authority and data scope are made explicit.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Preserve the actor-scope context and, on a future edit, say unqualified all users explicitly so the rejected shorthand cannot be mistaken for a universal prohibition.

ballot_rationales.rationale: The token all is part of the quoted vague actor label ‘all users’; the sentence rejects that unsafe label and does not quantify a universal implementation or authorization action.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Role and trust-boundary analysis where a vague umbrella actor label is being offered as authorization evidence.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Replace umbrella labels with explicit anonymous, authenticated, tenant, support, service, or external actors and their server-enforced scopes.

ballot_rationales.rationale: The absolute token appears inside the quoted anti-pattern "all users". In full context the sentence rejects four unsafe identity shortcuts; it does not prescribe one unconditional identity mechanism for every actor or event.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies when user-role-identification evaluates actor, service-identity, support, or webhook trust boundaries.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Keep the anti-pattern scoped to identity analysis and require explicit policy or authenticated provenance for the affected boundary.

ballot_rationales.rationale: Limiting the decision portion of the handoff to triggered catalog entries prevents checklist dumping and invented work while preserving task-local implementation evidence.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Backend-change-builder task mode after one or more proactive trigger rows have been activated by the actual changed path.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Still include the required diff, mapped validation, unverified scope, and residual risk; do not omit non-catalog evidence required by the task contract.

ballot_rationales.rationale: This is a scoped output rule for the proactive-trigger catalog: recording only decisions whose concrete signal fired avoids turning conditional security, consistency, migration, and reliability escalators into a mandatory backend checklist.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Backend implementation using this trigger Reference after one or more listed hidden-risk signals are present in the changed path.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Retain the normal implementation result, validation, risk, and handoff evidence; add a newly discovered risk to the triggered set before omitting or routing it.

ballot_rationales.rationale: The output restriction follows the Reference's trigger catalog: an implementation handoff should report decisions activated by the current change, not copy unrelated capability guidance. This preserves progressive disclosure while leaving actual diff and validation evidence visible.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies after backend-change-builder maps the current change signals to triggered backend decisions and validations.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Record every triggered decision and its evidence; reroute or reopen analysis when a new risk signal appears.

ballot_rationales.rationale: Each selected security risk needs accountable ownership and a containment or rollback outcome; otherwise the output can enumerate exposure without assigning an executable response boundary.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: The selected secret, supply-chain, or cloud risk fields in the security-privacy-gate output contract after a mode closure has been chosen.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Apply the rule only to risks actually selected from evidence, and state unknown or unavailable containment honestly rather than inventing a control.

ballot_rationales.rationale: Once a security risk is selected, leaving it without an accountable owner and a stated containment or rollback outcome creates an unowned release and incident-response gap.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Security or privacy gate closure for a risk selected from the inspected trust, secret, supply-chain, cloud, data, or tool-authority boundary.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: State when rollback is unavailable, identify containment or forward-fix handling, and keep untested exposure and the next owner explicit.

ballot_rationales.rationale: The quantifier is bounded by "selected risk" and enforces closure completeness for that selected set. Omitting an owner or containment or rollback outcome would leave an activated security risk without accountable treatment.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies only to risks selected by security-privacy-gate for the current change.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Keep selection evidence explicit and fail the gate when any selected risk lacks an owner or containment or rollback outcome.

ballot_rationales.rationale: The sentence negates exhaustive per-occurrence logging and explicitly qualifies the guidance as a default. Every is the rejected object, not an unconditional coverage command.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Logging selection after frequency, cardinality, operational purpose, and platform policy have been evaluated for the affected signal.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Keep evidence-based exceptions for audit or domain events, and calibrate detection for negated every-statements that also carry a by-default qualifier.

ballot_rationales.rationale: The clause is expressly qualified by ‘by default’; it rejects unexamined per-occurrence logging, not every-event logging when audit, security, diagnostic, or policy evidence requires it.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Logging selection where frequency, cardinality, retention, and diagnostic purpose have not yet justified per-occurrence emission.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Permit bounded per-occurrence events when required; otherwise select aggregation, sampling, rate control, metrics, traces, tests, or no new signal from evidence.

ballot_rationales.rationale: The phrase negates exhaustive logging and is further qualified by "by default". It therefore establishes neither an unconditional requirement to log every occurrence nor an unconditional prohibition on justified per-occurrence logging.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies when logging-design-gate chooses event placement, cardinality, sampling, and aggregation for the current risk.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Select per-occurrence logging only with risk and volume evidence; otherwise use aggregation, sampling, or state-transition records.

ballot_rationales.rationale: A cache key that omits an input capable of changing the cached result can return behavior from an incompatible build context, so completeness is a correctness invariant here.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: CI or build caching where current source evidence shows that an input can change the behavior or artifact represented by the cached entry.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Derive key material from proven behavior-affecting inputs, exclude volatile irrelevant values, and retain a full-suite or cache-bypass fallback.

ballot_rationales.rationale: For a reused build cache to be correct, every input capable of changing the cached result must participate in identity; omitting one permits stale or cross-context artifact reuse.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: CI/CD cache reuse for deterministic build, generated, dependency, or test outputs whose behavior-affecting inputs can be enumerated and safely represented.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Use safe digests or immutable versions rather than secret values, and disable reuse when an influential input cannot be keyed or made hermetic.

ballot_rationales.rationale: A cache key is unsound when an input capable of changing the cached behavior is omitted. The quantifier is professionally necessary but scoped to behavior-affecting inputs of the selected CI or build cache, not to every repository input.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies to a selected CI or build cache after its behavior-affecting inputs and invalidation boundary have been identified.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Document the input map and use a conservative cache miss or full rebuild when the invalidation boundary is uncertain.

ballot_rationales.rationale: The required re-review stage is derived from the stage that raised the finding, so the rule preserves independent ownership without imposing one fixed review pipeline.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Repair and re-review of a blocking finding where the originating review stage and its evidence boundary are known.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Name the exact originating stage and affected scope, and avoid rerunning unrelated gates that the failure mechanism did not invalidate.

ballot_rationales.rationale: Repair closure needs the responsible review stage named so the changed artifact returns to the gate that found the defect instead of receiving an unrelated or partial re-review.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: A blocking finding mapped to repair in a staged implementation, contract, security, architecture, or test review.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Name the affected stage and scope, pass the latest diff and fresh evidence, and require independent re-review before approval.

ballot_rationales.rationale: The sentence requires the handoff to name the review stage affected by a repair. That stage-specific obligation prevents an implementation repair from bypassing the independent gate that originally raised the finding.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies when ai-code-review-refactor returns a repair or re-review plan for an identified finding.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Name the responsible re-review stage and keep completion blocked until that stage supplies fresh evidence.

ballot_rationales.rationale: Risk-selected field emission keeps the security closure bounded to evidence and prevents an agent from fabricating secret, dependency, or cloud analysis that was never triggered.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: The security-privacy-gate output contract after secret, supply-chain, or cloud risks have been selected from the actual affected boundary.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Always retain the chosen mode closure and shared proof limits, while omitting only risk-specific fields whose triggering boundary is absent.

ballot_rationales.rationale: The restriction is local to risk-specific output fields after the mandatory mode closure; it prevents irrelevant checklist expansion while preserving evidence for every risk actually selected.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Security gate output after the current scope has selected concrete secret, dependency, supply-chain, or cloud risks.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Expand the selected-risk set when evidence exposes another reachable risk, and always retain mode closure, proof limits, residual exposure, and next ownership.

ballot_rationales.rationale: The field restriction is explicitly bounded to secrets, supply-chain, and cloud risks selected for the current change. It prevents an output contract from expanding into an irrelevant security catalog while preserving complete fields for every activated risk.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies to the secrets, supply-chain, and cloud section after security-privacy-gate selects risks for the current change.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Keep the risk-selection rationale visible and add fields when newly observed evidence activates another risk.

ballot_rationales.rationale: The HTTP codes are routing vocabulary in the Skill's Use when selector list. They neither prescribe returned statuses nor establish a fixed operational threshold.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: The network-protocol-gateway-usage Registry Trigger where 502, 503, and 504 identify gateway-failure tasks that may require this Skill.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Keep the codes as selector examples and exclude routing-trigger lists from fixed-status policy findings unless a clause actually commands a response status.

ballot_rationales.rationale: The status codes are routing vocabulary in the Skill’s Registry Trigger, alongside proxy and trace terms; no clause assigns those responses, thresholds, retries, or policy outcomes.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Skill selection when observed gateway behavior includes HTTP 502, 503, or 504 responses.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Derive any response mapping and retry behavior from the actual client-to-origin contract, and re-triage a future prescriptive status rule separately.

ballot_rationales.rationale: The numeric HTTP status codes are Registry trigger vocabulary used to route gateway failure work. They do not set a fixed success threshold, timeout, retry count, or status policy, so the fixed-duration-threshold-status detector family does not apply to the complete context.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies only to discovery and routing for network-protocol-gateway-usage when gateway or upstream failure signals include these statuses.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Keep status codes as routing signals only and require the loaded Reference to derive retry or failure behavior from protocol and system evidence.

ballot_rationales.rationale: Kubernetes names the owning Skill's runtime domain and the subject of its output contract. The sentence does not select Kubernetes as a vendor for otherwise platform-neutral work.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: The kubernetes-gateway output contract, and only after the task has crossed a Kubernetes workload, route, identity, health, capacity, or rollout boundary.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Do not route this Skill outside its cluster boundary, and continue deriving subordinate mechanisms from current platform policy rather than from the Kubernetes name alone.

ballot_rationales.rationale: Kubernetes names the already-selected capability and its scoped output record; the sentence does not mandate Kubernetes as a vendor or platform choice for unrelated runtime work.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: A task already inside the kubernetes-gateway trigger boundary because Kubernetes workload, route, identity, health, capacity, or rollout behavior changes.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Keep pipeline, image, migration, and non-cluster work outside this capability, and derive cluster mechanisms from current policy and workload consequences.

ballot_rationales.rationale: Kubernetes names the owning Skill's subject and routed runtime boundary; the Output Contract does not select Kubernetes for a context-free problem. The vendor-tool detector therefore mistakes owner terminology for a prescriptive fixed-tool choice.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies only after kubernetes-gateway is routed for a change that already affects Kubernetes workload, routing, identity, health, capacity, scheduling, or rollout behavior.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Preserve the anti-trigger boundary and do not use this Output Contract to recommend Kubernetes where no Kubernetes change signal exists.

ballot_rationales.rationale: The dispatch-only control plane must pass task-local routed guidance instead of ingesting a full Skill or Reference catalog; preloading would blur role boundaries and consume context without task evidence.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Main Control Agent scheduling and Skill routing, immediately after selection through the named professional-skill router and before bounded task dispatch.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Interpret index and catalog as Skill or Reference routing collections; the explicitly named router remains allowed, and task-local References remain available through dispatch.

ballot_rationales.rationale: For the dispatch-only control agent, index inspection and catalog preloading violate the role boundary and JIT-loading contract by importing unselected implementation knowledge into routing.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Main-control dispatch after the professional router has selected task-local ownership and before any source or Reference inspection.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Route source, index, and catalog discovery to a bounded analysis agent; pass only selected task-local Skills and named References to implementers.

ballot_rationales.rationale: The prohibition protects the Main Control Agent's dispatch-only and just-in-time context boundary. Inspecting an index or preloading a catalog would defeat exact Reference routing, inflate always-loaded context, and blur worker ownership.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies to Main Control Agent scheduling after a primary Professional Skill and any named Layer 3 guidance have been selected.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Load only exact named Layer 3 guidance and return to analysis or routing when a new risk requires another bounded Reference.

ballot_rationales.rationale: One primary Professional Skill establishes unambiguous task ownership; the router still permits targeted Layer 3 guidance and a separate Review Skill, so the count does not erase supporting expertise.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Per-task Main Control Agent routing through the professional-skill router after the work has been classified or decomposed into bounded tasks.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Decompose composite work into bounded tasks, then allow the router's targeted Layer 3 and Review Skills without assigning competing primary owners to one task.

ballot_rationales.rationale: Exactly one primary Professional Skill establishes unambiguous task-local decision ownership; supporting Skills and Layer 3 guidance remain routable without creating competing primary owners.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Each bounded task-agent assignment after routing has identified its dominant professional responsibility and acceptance boundary.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Split genuinely independent multi-owner work into separate task capsules or DAG nodes, and name supporting Skills without promoting them to co-primary ownership.

ballot_rationales.rationale: One primary Professional Skill establishes a single professional decision owner for a task slice, while named Foundation or Domain References may supplement it. The count is an architectural ownership constraint, not an arbitrary fixed threshold.
ballot_rationales.authority_or_condition: Applies when the Main Control Agent assigns the professional owner for one executable task slice through the professional-skill router.
ballot_rationales.mitigation: Keep singular primary ownership, add only routed supporting guidance, and re-evaluate the contract if explicit multi-primary composition is introduced.

limitations: This majority is authoring lifecycle evidence only.
It cannot satisfy readability or professional-completeness formal attestations.
The record contains no generated single-source-of-truth disposition entries.
A rewrite majority requires a source edit before any resolved governance entry can exist.
